description: Monthly bloom observations for A Beds (Block Plan) recorded during volunteer garden walks (2021–2025). The A Beds officially opened August 2021. Each entry captures what a volunteer observed on or near the 15th of each month. Status values: not_blooming, budding, peak, fading.

observations.notes: First season — modest bloom on newly planted monarda. Pale lavender flowers with spotted lips. Very few other plants blooming yet.
Brilliant orange. First monarch caterpillar observed July 18. Garden just opened to public.
Spherical white heads very striking. Visitors frequently ask what this unusual plant is.
Spikes forming rapidly. First-year plants shorter than expected (about 2.5 ft).
Full bloom. Monarchs visiting daily. Spikes opening top-to-bottom as expected.
Dense bloom on first-year 'Fatal Attraction'. Black stems very distinctive. Bumblebees active all day.
Seed heads forming. Blue-green summer color very distinctive.
Popcorn fragrance from seed heads very noticeable in warm weather. Fine texture beautiful.
First bloom — 'Sahin's Early Flowerer' living up to its name. Reflexed petals distinctive.
Vivid violet-purple. Monarchs stopping before Lake Erie crossing. 6+ monarchs counted Sept 14.
Buds forming on 'October Skies'. Will carry the garden into fall.
Bloom finished by May. Now in spectacular golden-orange fall color. Best fall foliage in the entire garden.
Full bloom — sky-blue daisies covering the plants. Last monarchs of the season visiting Oct 5–8.
Copper-orange fall color peak. Silver seed tufts glowing in afternoon light.
Star-shaped blue buds forming. Plants much larger in second year.
Pale blue flowers open. Feathery foliage very distinctive. Sphinx moth observed visiting at dusk.
Strongest bloom yet in second year. Pale lavender with purple-spotted lower lip. Square stems confirmed.
First strong bloom of 'Hummelo'. Dense violet spikes very neat and upright. Bumblebees working it constantly.
Emerged mid-May, buds forming by June 10 as expected for this late riser.
Full orange bloom. Monarch caterpillars found July 12. Great blue lobelia accent blooming alongside — stunning blue-orange combo.
Larger plants in year 2. Blue-green stems very striking. Many native bee species visiting spherical heads.
Silver bracts glowing. Counting bee species: identified 18 distinct species on the mountain mint pocket alone on July 22.
Tall spikes forming — 4+ feet in year 2. Expected peak by July 28.
Magnificent — spikes over 4.5 feet. Monarchs and swallowtails on every spike. Top-to-bottom bloom sequence clearly visible.
Very long bloom period in second year. Black stems and dark centers very distinctive from 'Fatal Attraction'. Goldfinch families visiting.
Gold-to-russet bicolor flowers at their best. Branching intensely — a cloud of color.
Buds forming, bloom expected late August.
Popcorn fragrance very strong this year. Fine texture provides beautiful contrast with bold forbs.
Deep violet-purple at peak. Rigid wiry stems undamaged by heavy winds Sept 8. Monarchs present.
Blue accent very striking in the coneflower block. White stripe on lower lip visible up close.
October Skies at full bloom. Fragrant foliage confirmed by crushing a leaf. Last migrating monarchs Oct 3.
Golden-orange fall foliage spectacular — the entire block transformed. Best fall display in the garden.
Blue flower buds visible by April 18. Large established mounds — plants now at full size.
Beautiful pale blue stars. Feathery foliage mounds now 3 feet wide. Milky sap confirmed in broken stem.
Peak bloom mid-May. Spotted lower lip very visible on close inspection. Square stems — classic mint family.
'Hummelo' at full bloom. Very compact and upright. Bumblebee count: 12 individuals on one plant June 10.
Brilliant orange. Monarch caterpillars confirmed July 9 and July 21. Certified waystation benefits clearly visible.
Fully established plants — 4.5 feet tall. Blue-green stems and spherical heads unmistakable. Visitors very curious about this plant.
Silver bracts luminous. Total bee species counted: 23 on mountain mint pocket in 30-minute observation July 19.
Best season yet — spikes 5 feet tall. Top-to-bottom bloom sequence textbook perfect. Monarchs abundant.
'Fatal Attraction' very consistent bloomer. Dark stems and near-black buds very distinctive from standard Echinacea.
Extremely heavy bloom — hundreds of flowers per plant. Reflexed petals in gold to russet bicolor.
Vivid violet-purple — among the richest colors in the entire garden. 15+ monarchs counted Sept 10.
Blue accent very strong. White stripe on lower lip clearly visible. Bumblebees are primary visitors — their tongues fit perfectly.
Sky-blue daisies in full bloom. Aromatic foliage — warm mint-herbal scent when crushed. Last monarchs Oct 6.
Full copper-orange fall color. Silver seed tufts spectacular in low October light.
Pale blue flowers at peak. Largest mounds yet — some over 3.5 feet wide. Golden fall color anticipated.
Good bloom. Pale lavender spotted flowers. Confirmed earliest-blooming monarda in the garden.
'Hummelo' very reliable. Dense violet spikes again. Confirmed 6–8 week bloom season.
Orange peak bloom. Monarch caterpillars July 7 and July 29. Seed pods forming on early flowers.
Silver bracts covering the pocket. 30-min observation July 14: 28 individual bees of at least 15 species.
Excellent season. Monarchs visiting daily in August. Bloom sequence top-to-bottom clearly observable.
Dense prolific bloom. Dark seed heads forming on earliest flowers. Goldfinch activity noted.
Buds forming mid-August. Earlier than previous years — may be due to warm summer.
Earlier peak than usual (August into September). Intense violet-purple. Monarch migration active.
Blue accent blooming strongly. Bumblebees the primary visitor — fit precisely to the flower tube.
'October Skies' covering itself with blue daisies. Aromatic foliage confirmed. Final monarch Oct 9.
Fall foliage spectacular — entire block glowing golden-orange. Best perennial fall color in the garden.
Blue buds visible April 20. Plants fully established, among the largest in the block.
Pale blue star flowers at peak. Feathery mounds now full-size. Outstanding plant.
Reliable and fragrant. Pale lavender spotted flowers confirmed earliest monarda in garden for fifth consecutive year.
